`/trips` now answers a bad `day` with a 400 and a JSON error saying what's wrong, instead of a 500 and a traceback. I checked it by calling the app directly with both values from your access log plus a few others; there's no test suite in the project, so nothing else was run.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `day=2026-09-31` | 400 `invalid day '2026-09-31': no such calendar date` |
| `day=14/09/2026` | 400 `invalid day '14/09/2026': expected format YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `day=` or no `day` at all | 400 `missing 'day' parameter; expected /trips?day=YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `day=2026-09-14` | 200, same summary as before |

The missing/empty case wasn't in your examples, but it hit the same ValueError and 500, so I covered it too.

The fix is a small `day_problem()` check in `app.py`, run before the summary is built; `trips.py` is untouched.

One thing I left alone: compact ISO forms like `day=20260914` still return 200, as they did before. If you want strictly `YYYY-MM-DD` only, that's a one-line tightening — say so and I'll add it.

The date picker is still sending these values, so the dashboard will now get 400s where it got 500s; the picker itself needs its own fix.
